title: SpaceX Faces First Major Test as 911 Million Shares Unlock After Record IPO
excerpt: The lockup expiry more than doubles the company's public float, creating a critical pressure point for Elon Musk's space and AI venture that has lost half its value since going public.
body:
• Up to 911.5 million SpaceX shares become eligible for sale Thursday, more than doubling the stock's public float from less than 5% to roughly 12%.
  • The stock has fallen nearly 50% from its June high and 20% below its $135 IPO price, closing at $108.27 after a 14% drop Wednesday.
  • SpaceX reported a 92% jump in Q2 revenue and is targeting $100 billion in annualized revenue by year-end.
  • Elon Musk's 42% stake remains locked up until June 2027 under a separate one-year agreement.

SpaceX's closely watched first lockup expiry hits Thursday, freeing up to 911.5 million shares for sale and delivering what brokers are calling the most anticipated lockup event in IPO history.

The unlocking more than doubles the number of shares available for public trading in Elon Musk's space and artificial intelligence company, which executed the largest IPO ever on June 12 but has seen its stock slide nearly 50% from its post-listing peak.

"This has to be the most talked-about lockup in the history of IPO lockups."

— Robert Hackel, CEO, R.F. Lafferty & Co.

What's Unlocking

SpaceX went public with less than 5% of its 13.6 billion outstanding shares available for trading — an unusually small float even by mega-IPO standards. Thursday's release brings the float to approximately 12%, with the eligible shares currently worth around $123 billion based on recent trading levels.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=eaMDArRaAHo

The staggered lockup structure is itself unusual. Rather than a single 180-day cliff, SpaceX's underwriters scheduled releases in tranches running through mid-2027. Thursday marks the first wave: rank-and-file employees and some early investors can sell, while executive officers remain locked up until after fourth-quarter earnings. Musk, who controls about 42% of the company, cannot sell until one year after the IPO.

Sell Pressure Meets Strong Fundamentals

Employees who acquired shares at pre-IPO valuations — often a fraction of the $135 listing price — are sitting on substantial gains despite the recent selloff. SpaceX closed at $108.27 Wednesday after falling nearly 14%, its second-worst day on record. The company's Tuesday earnings report revealed larger-than-expected capital expenditures on artificial intelligence, compounding pressure from the approaching lockup date.

"You have a few different things triggering volatile action in the name, all happening at the same time," Ryan Lee, senior vice president for product and strategy at Direxion, told CNN. "With these employee share unlocks, you're going to have natural sellers entering the market. These are people who've held the stock far before it was printing at $135 on the IPO."

The selling pressure comes despite a strong earnings debut. SpaceX reported a 92% jump in second-quarter revenue, and CEO Bret Johnsen told analysts the company is on track to reach $100 billion in annualized revenue by year-end.

Brokers expect heavy selling. Hackel said he has been fielding calls from pre-IPO investors eager to cash out and redeploy into privately traded stock in other IPO candidates such as Anthropic, OpenAI, and Anduril Industries. "You are going to see a lot of exits," he said.

Not Everyone Is Heading for the Door

Gabriel Shahin, founder of Falcon Wealth Planning, said his contacts among SpaceX insiders show none are eager to sell. "They're long-term believers in SpaceX, and as a result we tend to be more bullish on insiders also not selling and what that says about the stock," he said.

But Shahin acknowledged that each upcoming lockup expiry date is likely to amplify turbulence. Options prices on SpaceX shares have reached levels he described as "sheer insanity," making it difficult for investors to hedge against further declines.

Nasdaq 100 Implications

The increased float carries index consequences. SpaceX currently holds a roughly 1% weighting in the Nasdaq 100, which it joined earlier this summer. After the index rebalances in September, that weight could rise above 3.5% based on the expanded float, according to TD Securities. A larger weighting means greater influence on the index's performance — and more passive fund buying.

What's Next

Additional lockup expirations are scheduled for August 20, followed by releases in September and October. After third-quarter earnings, another 28% of pre-IPO shares will unlock. By December 8, restrictions will have lifted on about 40% of total shares outstanding. The remaining 60%, including Musk's stake and institutional holdings from Founders Fund, Craft Ventures, and Alphabet, stays locked until mid-2027.

"These lockups will be an interesting test of the commitment of early investors to stand by the company for the long haul," said Andrew Chanin, CEO of Procure AM, which manages the Procure Space ETF.
